english.title: Without the consent of the owner / occupier of land search for / pursue deer with intent to take / kill / injure
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), whilst on land, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), and without the consent of the owner or occupier of the land or other lawful authority,

(A)_[searched for]_
(B)_[pursued]_

deer with the intention of taking, killing or injuring the same
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(2)(b) and 9 of the Deer Act 1991.

english.notes:
(i) See section 1(3) for exceptions.
(ii) If more than one deer is involved in a single offence the fine shall be determined as if the person convicted has been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each deer.
(iii) Time limit on Prosecutions - Section 9(3) of the Deer Act 1991 provides that proceedings for an offence may be brought within the period of 6 months beginning with the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the prosecutor to warrant the proceedings came to his knowledge.
(iv) Forfeiture - Section 13 of the Act provides the courts with powers to order the forfeiture of vehicles, animals, weapons and other things and to disqualify offenders from holding a game dealers licence.
(v) Disqualification - Section 13(2) of the Act provides that where a person is convicted of this offence, the court (in addition to any other penalty), may disqualify that person for holding or obtaining a licence to deal in game for such period as the court thinks fit and may cancel any firearm or shotgun certificate held by him.
